weather_line: Crisp in the hollows · hat weather, apparently · ducks proliferating

stories.headline: Second Duck Confirmed; Hat Matches Nothing on Record; Witness Describes 'A Purposeful Shape' and Then Goes Quiet
body: A second charmed rubber duck appeared on the Jeep overnight Thursday, discovered Friday morning at approximately seven-forty. Like its predecessor, it is wearing a hat. Unlike its predecessor, the hat is different: where the first was a small flat cap of what Steve has described as 'confident construction,' the second presents a tiny wide-brim affair in a warm amber felt, fixed at a jaunty angle and showing no signs of magical instability whatsoever. Both hats are, by all expert assessment, well-made.

One witness has come forward — a Mr. T. Finch of Hollow Branch Lane, who was walking his owl at the relevant hour and reports seeing 'a purposeful shape' near the Jeep from a distance of approximately forty yards. When pressed for further detail, Mr. Finch went quiet, looked at the middle distance for a moment, and said only that the shape 'seemed to know what it was doing.' He offered this not as a complaint but as an observation he found privately reassuring. He has since declined all follow-up contact.

The Ministry's Duck Provenance Office — a department that did not exist a fortnight ago and has since acquired a cork board, three string lines, and a junior analyst named Pemwick — has opened a formal inquiry. Pemwick has noted that the two hats, while different in style, share the same stitch count. The Jeep has been examined for residual charm traces and found to be, in Pemwick's words, 'very clean and also quite a good Jeep.' The Duck Bandit has not claimed responsibility. The trail awaits.

stories.headline: Friday's Sole Remaining Dispute Resolved Before the Relevant Goblin Finished Reading It Aloud
body: A Friday morning dispute — filed under Contested Appraisal, Clause Seven, with a supplementary grievance attached on a separate scroll — was resolved by Christine at ten past nine, which is to say approximately fifteen seconds before Senior Clerk Ragwich completed his formal reading of the opening paragraph.

Ragwich is understood to have paused mid-sentence, looked up, and found the matter already settled. He has since submitted a procedural note requesting that the Gringotts Charter be amended to allow Christine to resolve disputes before they are officially opened, on grounds of institutional efficiency. The Goblin Senior Council has taken this under advisement, which in goblin terms means they are considering it quite seriously and will not say so for at least a fortnight.
The client left satisfied. Ragwich filed everything correctly. Christine moved on to her second coffee. All told, a Friday.

stories.headline: Ministry's 'Wholesome, Not Misc.' Registry Receives First Inquiry From Abroad; Quoyne Replies Promptly and With Evident Pride
body: Word of the 'Wholesome, Not Misc.' registry — now containing two formally inscribed entries and a third divider held in reserve — has apparently reached the Department of International Magical Cooperation, which dispatched a brief query Friday asking whether the registry's classification rubric was available for cross-departmental consultation.

Senior Archivist Quoyne replied within the hour. His response, by all accounts, ran to three paragraphs: one confirming the rubric's availability, one summarising the two existing entries with concise dignity, and one noting that the shelf housing the registry is plumb to within a sixteenth of an inch and has been since installation. The third paragraph was not strictly requested but was, all parties agree, appropriate.
Quoyne has since straightened the shelf label. It was already straight. He has confirmed this twice.

stories.headline: Friday Evening Briefing: Biscuit Tin in Fourth Consecutive Fixed Position; Lucy Reportedly 'Considering Her Options'; Jersey Has No Options, Is Comfortable, Carries On
body: The biscuit tin has not moved in four days. Household analysts, who have now begun referring to this period as 'The Stability,' are divided on its meaning: the optimistic camp holds that the tin has found its home; the cautious camp notes that Lucy has been sitting near the kitchen archway each evening in a posture they describe as 'architecturally neutral but emotionally active.'

Ellie spent part of Friday afternoon engaged with her reflection in the back of a decorative cauldron, apparently under the impression that it was a new dog who had come to visit and was being very polite about the whole thing. She offered it a toy. The toy was not accepted. She retrieved it, waited a respectful interval, and offered it again. Steve witnessed this exchange and has filed no report, as he didn't have the heart.

Jersey, untroubled by the existential dimensions of any of this, located the warmest available patch of late-afternoon light, turned twice, and settled. It is Friday. The week is done. He has done his part.

familiars_corner: Lucy: Was seen this evening standing very still in the kitchen, looking at nothing in particular, for approximately four minutes. When the biscuit tin was checked afterwards, it was in exactly the same position. Exactly.
Ellie: Made a new friend in the cauldron reflection today and is hopeful it will come back tomorrow. She has left a toy out, just in case. This is very kind of her.
Jersey: It is Friday evening, which means it is lap time, which means it is always lap time, which means Jersey was right all along and is now extremely comfortable about it.
founding_editor_note: Two ducks, two hats, one witness who won't talk — that's a good story. You don't rush a good story. You let it find the level. — D.

in_brief.sport: Gringotts Strongwitch Invitational postponed pending vault rescheduling; reigning champion unavailable for comment as she is already back at her desk.
in_brief.forecast: Friday night: clear, cool, and quiet in the hollows. Saturday: the Jeep is watching for developments. The ducks are saying nothing.

storyline_updates.title: The Duck Bandit Returns
storyline_updates.summary: Day 2: A second duck has appeared, wearing a different but equally well-made hat — a wide-brim amber felt, jaunty angle. One witness (T. Finch) reports a 'purposeful shape' near the Jeep but has gone quiet. The Ministry's Duck Provenance Office, staffed by junior analyst Pemwick, has opened a formal inquiry and noted that both hats share the same stitch count, suggesting a single maker. The Jeep is clean of all charm traces. Day 3 should develop a new clue — perhaps Pemwick finds something significant in the stitch pattern, or a third duck appears with a different hat that completes some kind of set or sequence, or someone in the broader Jeep community recognises the hat style as specific to a known (if elusive) figure.
